newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says talking to EU on Northwest, no fine yet.
newsitem.headline: KLM says talking to EU on Northwest, no fine yet.

text.p: Dutch national carrier KLM said on Tuesday it was in talks with the European Commission on its transatlantic tie-up with Northwest Airlines, but said fines were not yet at issue.

"KLM was approached by the European Commission as part of its investigation into airline alliances and is currently in talks with the European Commission on that...we have not yet received a (formal) decision from the EU," spokeswoman Marjolein Wenting said.
A European Commission official said earlier the Commission was due to threaten KLM with a daily fine if it did not provide details of its seven-year link-up with Northwest.

The Commission said last July it would mount a competition probe into a range of tie-ups between European and U.S. carriers after British Airways unveiled plans for a mega partnership deal with AMR Corp's American Airlines.
KLM's Wenting said that before the Commission could fine parties for failing to provide information it had to send a formal decision demanding information in writing.
So far KLM had only received a request rather than a decision and was in talks with the Commission about what it wanted to know, Wenting said.
She declined to comment on the progress of the talks.

KLM's highly lucrative partnership with its 19 percent-owned partner Northwest Airlines dates back to 1989. It was the first to gain immunity from U.S. antitrust law, enabling the two airlines to operate as a single company on transatlantic routes.
